questions.questionText: When an equimolar mixture of benzaldehyde ($\text{PhCHO}$) and 4-methoxybenzaldehyde ($p\text{-anisaldehyde}$, $p-\text{CH}_3\text{O}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CHO}$) is heated with catalytic potassium cyanide ($\text{KCN}$) in aqueous ethanol under reflux, which of the following is isolated as the major crossed benzoin condensation product?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In the benzoin condensation, the initial nucleophilic addition of cyanide ion ($\text{CN}^-$) occurs preferentially at the more electrophilic carbonyl carbon. Benzaldehyde has a significantly more electrophilic carbonyl carbon than 4-methoxybenzaldehyde because the strong electron-donating resonance effect ($+M$) of the $p$-methoxy group delocalizes electron density into the aromatic ring and diminishes the partial positive charge on the carbonyl carbon of 4-methoxybenzaldehyde.

Step 2: Consequently, cyanide ion attacks benzaldehyde preferentially to generate the cyanohydrin intermediate, which undergoes proton transfer to form the active nucleophilic acyl anion equivalent (the carbanion $\text{Ph}-\text{C}^-(\text{OH})-\text{CN}$).

Step 3: This benzaldehyde-derived carbanion then attacks the carbonyl group of the remaining aldehyde present in the mixture. Attack on 4-methoxybenzaldehyde forms the crossed tetrahedral intermediate $\text{Ph}-\text{C}(\text{OH})(\text{CN})-\text{CH}(\text{O}^-)-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-p-\text{OCH}_3$.

Step 4: Proton transfer followed by expulsion of cyanide ion ($\text{CN}^-$) regenerates the carbonyl group at the phenyl carbon while the 4-methoxyphenyl carbon remains as a secondary alcohol, producing 2-hydroxy-2-(4-methoxyphenyl)-1-phenylethan-1-one ($\text{Ph}-\text{CO}-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-p-\text{OCH}_3$, $C$).

Therefore, 2-hydroxy-2-(4-methoxyphenyl)-1-phenylethan-1-one is the major product. The regioisomer with the carbonyl adjacent to the anisyl group requires initial cyanide attack on the deactivated aldehyde, symmetrical bis-anisoin is formed only in minor amounts, and the dione requires subsequent oxidation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the Baeyer-Villiger oxidation of two substituted acetophenones with trifluoroperacetic acid ($\text{CF}_3\text{CO}_3\text{H}$):
Reaction 1: 4-nitroacetophenone ($p-\text{NO}_2-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{COCH}_3$) reacts to form product $P$.
Reaction 2: 4-methoxyacetophenone ($p-\text{CH}_3\text{O}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{COCH}_3$) reacts to form product $Q$.
Which of the following correctly identifies the structures of products $P$ and $Q$?
options: A) $P$ is 4-nitrophenyl acetate, and $Q$ is 4-methoxyphenyl acetate
B) $P$ is methyl 4-nitrobenzoate, and $Q$ is methyl 4-methoxybenzoate
C) $P$ is 4-nitrophenyl acetate, and $Q$ is methyl 4-methoxybenzoate
D) $P$ is methyl 4-nitrobenzoate, and $Q$ is 4-methoxyphenyl acetate
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In the Baeyer-Villiger oxidation of acetophenones ($\text{Ar}-\text{COCH}_3$), the two migrating candidates are the substituted aryl group ($\text{Ar}$) and the methyl group ($-\text{CH}_3$).

Step 2: Migration of an aryl group proceeds via a phenonium-like transition state where the aromatic ring donates electron density into the developing electron-deficient migration terminus. Therefore, electron-donating substituents strongly accelerate aryl migration, whereas electron-withdrawing substituents strongly retard it.

Step 3: In Reaction 2 with 4-methoxyacetophenone, the methoxy group is a powerful resonance electron-donor ($+M$). The $p$-methoxyphenyl group has a vastly higher migratory aptitude than a methyl group. Oxygen inserts between the aryl ring and the carbonyl carbon, producing 4-methoxyphenyl acetate ($Q$, $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-p-\text{OCH}_3$).

Step 4: In Reaction 1 with 4-nitroacetophenone, the nitro group exerts powerful $-M$ and $-I$ electron-withdrawing effects, drastically depleting electron density from the aromatic ring and destabilizing the migration transition state. This retards aryl migration so severely that its migratory aptitude drops below that of a methyl group! Consequently, the methyl group migrates preferentially, inserting oxygen between the carbonyl carbon and methyl group to yield methyl 4-nitrobenzoate ($P$, $p-\text{NO}_2-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{COOCH}_3$).

Therefore, $P$ is methyl 4-nitrobenzoate and $Q$ is 4-methoxyphenyl acetate. Option combinations assuming that aryl always migrates or methyl always migrates fail to recognize the dramatic reversal in migratory aptitude caused by the nitro group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Cyclohexanone is reacted with methylenetriphenylphosphorane ($\text{Ph}_3\text{P}=\text{CH}_2$, prepared in situ from methyltriphenylphosphonium bromide and $n$-butyllithium) in dry diethyl ether to afford an exocyclic alkene $A$. Alkene $A$ is subsequently subjected to hydroboration-oxidation by reaction with diborane ($\text{B}_2\text{H}_6$) in THF followed by alkaline hydrogen peroxide ($\text{H}_2\text{O}_2/\text{NaOH}$). What is the IUPAC name of the final alcohol $B$?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: The reaction of cyclohexanone with the unstabilized phosphorus ylide methylenetriphenylphosphorane ($\text{Ph}_3\text{P}=\text{CH}_2$) is an archetypal Wittig olefination. The ylide carbanion attacks the cyclohexanone carbonyl carbon, forming an oxaphosphetane that decomposes irreversibly with loss of triphenylphosphine oxide ($\text{Ph}_3\text{P}=\text{O}$) to replace the $\text{C}=\text{O}$ bond with an exocyclic $\text{C}=\text{CH}_2$ double bond, yielding methylenecyclohexane ($A$).

Step 2: Methylenecyclohexane ($A$) is then subjected to hydroboration-oxidation. Addition of borane ($\text{BH}_3$) across the carbon-carbon double bond is stereospecifically syn and regioselectively anti-Markovnikov.

Step 3: Boron preferentially binds to the less sterically hindered, less substituted terminal methylene carbon ($-\text{CH}_2-$), while hydrogen attaches to the fully substituted $\text{C}-1$ ring carbon, forming a trialkylborane intermediate.

Step 4: Oxidation with alkaline hydrogen peroxide ($\text{H}_2\text{O}_2/\text{NaOH}$) replaces the carbon-boron bond with a carbon-oxygen bond with complete retention of stereochemistry, yielding the primary alcohol cyclohexylmethanol ($B$, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$).

Therefore, cyclohexylmethanol is the final product. 1-methylcyclohexan-1-ol arises from Markovnikov hydration of the alkene, 2-methylcyclohexan-1-ol would require an endocyclic double bond, and cycloheptanol would require a ring expansion rearrangement.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Cinnamaldehyde ((2E)-3-phenylprop-2-enal, $\text{PhCH}=\text{CH}-\text{CHO}$) is treated with acetophenone ($\text{PhCOCH}_3$) in ethanol in the presence of dilute aqueous sodium hydroxide ($\text{NaOH}$) with gentle heating. What is the IUPAC name of the major conjugated condensation product obtained after dehydration?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In this crossed aldol condensation, acetophenone ($\text{PhCOCH}_3$) possesses three active $\alpha$-hydrogens on its methyl group, whereas cinnamaldehyde ($\text{PhCH}=\text{CH}-\text{CHO}$) has no enolizable $\alpha$-hydrogens adjacent to its formyl group.

Step 2: Sodium hydroxide abstracts a proton from the methyl group of acetophenone to generate the phenacyl enolate carbanion, $\text{Ph}-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2^-$.

Step 3: This enolate attacks the electrophilic formyl carbonyl carbon of cinnamaldehyde to form a $\beta$-hydroxy ketone intermediate: $\text{PhCH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}_2-\text{COPh}$.

Step 4: Under the reaction conditions, this intermediate undergoes base-promoted dehydration (loss of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$) to produce an extended, uninterrupted conjugated $\pi$-electron system connecting both phenyl rings across a conjugated diene-one framework: $\text{PhCH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{COPh}$.

Step 5: Numbering the carbon chain according to IUPAC rules, the principal functional group is the ketone carbonyl at $\text{C}-1$. The five-carbon chain extends to $\text{C}-5$, with double bonds between $\text{C}-2/\text{C}-3$ and $\text{C}-4/\text{C}-5$, and phenyl substituents at $\text{C}-1$ and $\text{C}-5$. Because both newly formed and existing double bonds adopt the thermodynamically favored trans geometry, the compound is (2E,4E)-1,5-diphenylpenta-2,4-dien-1-one ($B$).

Therefore, (2E,4E)-1,5-diphenylpenta-2,4-dien-1-one is the major product. (1E,4E)-1,5-diphenylpenta-1,4-dien-3-one has the carbonyl in the middle from acetone, (E)-1,3-diphenylprop-2-en-1-one is chalcone from benzaldehyde, and the alcohol represents an unformed carbonyl.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Methyl 4-oxocyclohexanecarboxylate is treated with 1.0 equivalent of sodium borohydride ($\text{NaBH}_4$) in methanol at 0°C to selectively reduce the ketone carbonyl group, followed by aqueous workup to afford compound $P$. Subsequent alkaline hydrolysis of the ester group in $P$ with aqueous sodium hydroxide ($\text{NaOH}$) followed by acidification with dilute hydrochloric acid yields the hydroxy acid $Q$. What is the total number of stereoisomers (geometrical cis/trans isomers) that exist for compound $Q$?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Methyl 4-oxocyclohexanecarboxylate contains both a ketone carbonyl at $\text{C}-4$ and an ester group at $\text{C}-1$. Sodium borohydride ($\text{NaBH}_4$) is a mild hydride donor that selectively reduces ketones and aldehydes in the presence of esters. Reduction of the $\text{C}-4$ ketone converts it into a secondary alcohol, producing methyl 4-hydroxycyclohexanecarboxylate ($P$).

Step 2: Saponification of the ester with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ followed by acidification hydrolyzes the methyl ester to a carboxylic acid, yielding 4-hydroxycyclohexanecarboxylic acid ($Q$, $\text{HO}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_9-\text{COOH}$).

Step 3: Analyze the stereochemistry of 4-hydroxycyclohexanecarboxylic acid:
- The molecule possesses a vertical plane of symmetry passing through carbon atoms $\text{C}-1$ and $\text{C}-4$ and their attached substituents ($-\text{COOH}$, $-\text{H}$, $-\text{OH}$, and $-\text{H}$).
- Because of this internal plane of symmetry, neither $\text{C}-1$ nor $\text{C}-4$ is an asymmetric chiral carbon center; the molecule is completely achiral and lacks optical activity.

Step 4: However, the substituents at $\text{C}-1$ and $\text{C}-4$ can be oriented on the same face or opposite faces of the cyclohexane chair/ring conformation, giving rise to exactly two diastereomeric geometrical isomers:
1. cis-4-hydroxycyclohexanecarboxylic acid (both $-\text{OH}$ and $-\text{COOH}$ groups on the same face of the ring)
2. trans-4-hydroxycyclohexanecarboxylic acid ($-\text{OH}$ and $-\text{COOH}$ groups on opposite faces of the ring)

Therefore, the total number of stereoisomers for compound $Q$ is exactly 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When benzaldehyde ($\text{PhCHO}$) is heated with concentrated aqueous sodium hydroxide ($\text{NaOH}$), a mixture of organic compounds $X$ is obtained. In contrast, when benzaldehyde is heated under reflux with a catalytic amount of potassium cyanide ($\text{KCN}$) in aqueous ethanol, a single organic compound $Y$ is obtained. What are the identities of $X$ and $Y$?
options: A) $X$ is benzoin; $Y$ is a mixture of benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate
B) $X$ is benzoic acid; $Y$ is mandelic acid
C) $X$ is a mixture of benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate; $Y$ is benzoin
D) $X$ is cinnamic acid; $Y$ is benzyl cyanide
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Benzaldehyde lacks $\alpha$-hydrogens adjacent to its carbonyl carbon and therefore cannot undergo aldol condensation in basic media.

Step 2: When heated with concentrated aqueous sodium hydroxide ($\text{NaOH}$, a strong Brønsted base and oxygen nucleophile), benzaldehyde undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction. Hydride transfer from a hydroxide-carbonyl tetrahedral intermediate to a second molecule of benzaldehyde disproportionates the starting material into an equimolar mixture of an oxidized product, sodium benzoate ($\text{PhCOONa}$), and a reduced product, benzyl alcohol ($\text{PhCH}_2\text{OH}$). Thus, mixture $X$ consists of benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate.

Step 3: When heated with catalytic potassium cyanide ($\text{KCN}$ in aqueous ethanol), cyanide ion acts as a specialized soft carbon nucleophile. Cyanide attacks the carbonyl carbon to form a cyanohydrin carbanion that undergoes umpolung (inversion of carbonyl polarity), enabling it to attack another molecule of benzaldehyde.

Step 4: Subsequent proton transfer and elimination of cyanide ion regenerates the catalyst and forms benzoin ($Y$, 2-hydroxy-1,2-diphenylethan-1-one, $\text{PhCH(OH)COPh}$).

Therefore, $X$ is a mixture of benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate, and $Y$ is benzoin. Interchanging the reagents fails to distinguish between the nucleophilic umpolung behavior of cyanide and the simple redox disproportionation promoted by hydroxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: An enantiomerically pure ketone, (3S)-3-phenylbutan-2-one, is treated with trifluoroperacetic acid ($\text{CF}_3\text{CO}_3\text{H}$) in dichloromethane. The reaction undergoes Baeyer-Villiger oxidation with complete regioselectivity. What is the absolute stereochemical configuration of the chiral center in the resulting ester product?
options: B) Inversion of configuration yielding (1R)-1-phenylethyl acetate
C) Retention of configuration yielding methyl (2S)-2-phenylpropanoate
D) Retention of configuration yielding (1S)-1-phenylethyl acetate
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In (3S)-3-phenylbutan-2-one ($\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-\text{CH(Ph)CH}_3$), the carbonyl carbon is flanked by a methyl group ($-\text{CH}_3$) and a secondary benzylic chiral group ((1S)-1-phenylethyl, $-\text{CH(Ph)CH}_3$).

Step 2: Migratory aptitude in Baeyer-Villiger oxidation follows: secondary alkyl/benzyl $\gg$ primary alkyl/methyl. Therefore, the (1S)-1-phenylethyl group migrates exclusively to the peroxy oxygen atom, inserting oxygen between the carbonyl carbon and the chiral benzylic center to form 1-phenylethyl acetate ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH(Ph)CH}_3$).

Step 3: The migration of the chiral group occurs via a concerted front-side intramolecular shift onto the adjacent oxygen atom with simultaneous displacement of the trifluoroacetate leaving group.

Step 4: Because the migrating carbon never becomes a free planar carbocation or radical, this concerted rearrangement proceeds with strict $100\%$ retention of stereochemical configuration at the migrating carbon center.

Step 5: Assigning Cahn-Ingold-Prelog priorities to the four substituents at the chiral carbon of the product ($-\text{OCOCH}_3 > -\text{Ph} > -\text{CH}_3 > -\text{H}$): The spatial arrangement of the groups is preserved, and the priority ranking of the oxygen-bearing group matches that of the original carbonyl group, confirming the absolute configuration remains (1S).

Therefore, the product is (1S)-1-phenylethyl acetate with complete retention of configuration. Racemization would require an unobserved free carbocation, and inversion would require an intermolecular backside substitution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: An organic compound containing two distinct carbonyl functions, 4-oxocyclohexanecarbaldehyde, is treated with 1.0 equivalent of ethane-1,2-dithiol in dry diethyl ether in the presence of catalytic boron trifluoride etherate ($\text{BF}_3\cdot\text{OEt}_2$). The resulting mono-dithioacetal intermediate is subsequently stirred with excess sodium borohydride ($\text{NaBH}_4$) in ethanol, followed by heating with active Raney Nickel. What is the major organic product obtained?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: 4-oxocyclohexanecarbaldehyde possesses two carbonyl groups: an aldehyde group ($-\text{CHO}$) and a ketone group (cyclohexanone $\text{C}=\text{O}$). Aldehyde carbonyls are less sterically hindered and possess higher electrophilicity than cyclic ketone carbonyls.

Step 2: In the presence of exactly 1.0 equivalent of ethane-1,2-dithiol and $\text{BF}_3\cdot\text{OEt}_2$, thioacetalization occurs chemoselectively at the aldehyde carbonyl to form a 1,3-dithiolane ring, yielding 4-(1,3-dithiolan-2-yl)cyclohexan-1-one.

Step 3: Treatment with $\text{NaBH}_4$ selectively reduces the unprotected ketone carbonyl to a secondary alcohol without affecting the dithiolane protecting group, producing 4-(1,3-dithiolan-2-yl)cyclohexan-1-ol.

Step 4: Subsequent heating with excess active Raney Nickel in ethanol brings about hydrogenolytic desulfurization (Mozingo desulfurization). Both carbon-sulfur bonds of the 1,3-dithiolane are cleaved and replaced by carbon-hydrogen bonds, converting the protected formyl group ($-\text{CH}(\text{S}-\text{CH}_2)_2$) directly into a methyl group ($-\text{CH}_3$).

Step 5: The resulting molecule is 4-methylcyclohexan-1-ol ($A$).

Therefore, 4-methylcyclohexan-1-ol is the major product. 4-(hydroxymethyl)cyclohexan-1-one represents protection at the wrong carbonyl, 1-methylcyclohexane-1,4-diol assumes an additional nucleophilic methylation, and cyclohexylmethanol incorrectly presumes loss of the ketone.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: During the Wittig reaction between an unstabilized phosphorus ylide ($\text{Ph}_3\text{P}=\text{CHCH}_3$) and an aldehyde ($\text{RCHO}$), what is the key neutral four-membered heterocyclic intermediate whose formation and subsequent cycloreversion governs the extrusion of the alkene?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In the modern mechanistic understanding of the Wittig reaction (confirmed by low-temperature $^{31}\text{P}$ NMR spectroscopy), the nucleophilic ylide carbanion attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon of the aldehyde.

Step 2: This addition rapidly and concertedly forms a neutral four-membered ring consisting of one phosphorus atom, one oxygen atom, and two carbon atoms, designated as a 1,2-oxaphosphetane.

Step 3: The 1,2-oxaphosphetane intermediate undergoes a stereospecific retro-[2+2] cycloreversion. The driving force for this ring opening is the formation of the exceptionally strong phosphorus-oxygen double bond in triphenylphosphine oxide ($\text{Ph}_3\text{P}=\text{O}$, bond dissociation energy $\approx 540\text{ kJ/mol}$), accompanied by the extrusion of the alkene ($\text{R}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$).

Step 4: Phosphonium betaine (an acyclic zwitterionic intermediate) was historically proposed by Georg Wittig, but extensive kinetic and spectroscopic studies have established that oxaphosphetanes are the actual observable resting intermediates, especially in non-polar solvents.

Therefore, 1,2-oxaphosphetane is the key four-membered intermediate. Phosphiranes are three-membered phosphorus heterocycles, and dioxaphospholanes are five-membered rings containing two oxygen atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Acetophenone ($\text{PhCOCH}_3$) and propiophenone ($\text{PhCOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$) are placed in separate flasks and treated with excess iodine and aqueous sodium hydroxide solution ($\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$). Let $n_1$ be the number of moles of yellow iodoform ($\text{CHI}_3$) precipitated from 1.0 mole of acetophenone, and let $n_2$ be the number of moles of iodoform precipitated from 1.0 mole of propiophenone. What is the numerical value of the expression $(10n_1 + n_2)$?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: The haloform reaction requires the presence of a methyl group directly bonded to a carbonyl group ($-\text{COCH}_3$) or a secondary alcohol with a methyl group ($-\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$) that can be oxidized in situ to a methyl carbonyl.

Step 2: Acetophenone ($\text{PhCOCH}_3$) contains a methyl ketone group. In the presence of excess $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{NaOH}$, all three $\alpha$-hydrogens of the methyl group are sequentially replaced by iodine to form 2,2,2-triiodo-1-phenylethan-1-one ($\text{PhCOCI}_3$). Hydroxide attack at the carbonyl carbon cleaves the triiodomethyl anion ($^-\text{CI}_3$), which rapidly abstracts a proton to precipitate 1.0 mole of yellow iodoform ($\text{CHI}_3$) per mole of acetophenone. Thus, $n_1 = 1$.

Step 3: Propiophenone ($\text{PhCOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$) contains an ethyl group bonded to the carbonyl carbon. It has two $\alpha$-hydrogens on a methylene carbon ($-\text{CH}_2-$). In the presence of $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$, $\alpha$-iodination occurs to give $\text{PhCOCH(I)}\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{PhCOCI}_2\text{CH}_3$. However, because there is no methyl group attached to the carbonyl, the leaving group upon nucleophilic attack would be a primary or secondary carbanion, which is an extremely poor leaving group and cannot cleave to form iodoform. Consequently, no iodoform precipitate forms. Thus, $n_2 = 0$.

Step 4: Evaluating the expression:
$$(10n_1 + n_2) = 10(1) + 0 = 10$$

Therefore, the numerical value is exactly 10.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the Wolff-Kishner reduction, a ketone or aldehyde is heated with hydrazine hydrate ($\text{NH}_2\text{NH}_2\cdot\text{H}_2\text{O}$) and potassium hydroxide ($\text{KOH}$) in a high-boiling solvent like diethylene glycol to reduce the carbonyl group to a methylene group ($-\text{CH}_2-$). What is the primary thermodynamic driving force that renders this multi-step reaction completely irreversible?
options: A) The high boiling point and coordinating ability of diethylene glycol
B) The precipitation of potassium carbonate from the alkaline reaction mixture
C) The irreversible extrusion of extremely stable dinitrogen gas ($\text{N}_2$) accompanied by a large increase in entropy
D) The oxidation of hydrazine to hydroxylamine by the carbonyl substrate
questions.explanation:
Step 1: The Wolff-Kishner reduction begins with condensation between the carbonyl compound and hydrazine to form a hydrazone intermediate, $\text{R}_2\text{C}=\text{N}-\text{NH}_2$.

Step 2: Under strongly basic conditions, hydroxide deprotonates the terminal nitrogen of the hydrazone, generating a resonance-stabilized diazenyl carbanion:
$$\text{R}_2\text{C}=\text{N}-\bar{\text{N}}\text{H} \longleftrightarrow \text{R}_2\bar{\text{C}}-\text{N}=\text{NH}$$
Protonation of the carbon atom by the solvent forms an alkyldiazene intermediate, $\text{R}_2\text{CH}-\text{N}=\text{NH}$.

Step 3: Deprotonation of the remaining nitrogen proton by base triggers a concerted bond reorganization in which the carbon-nitrogen bond is broken, an alkyl carbanion ($\text{R}_2\text{CH}^-$) is expelled, and molecular dinitrogen gas ($\text{N}_2$) is released:
$$\text{R}_2\text{CH}-\text{N}=\bar{\text{N}} \longrightarrow \text{R}_2\text{CH}^- + \text{N}_2\uparrow$$

Step 4: The formation of the exceptionally strong nitrogen-nitrogen triple bond in $\text{N}_2$ (bond dissociation energy $\approx 945\text{ kJ/mol}$) contributes a very large negative enthalpy change ($\Delta H^\circ \ll 0$). In addition, the generation of a gaseous product that escapes from the open reflux system provides a large positive entropy change ($\Delta S^\circ > 0$), making the Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G^\circ = \Delta H^\circ - T\Delta S^\circ$) overwhelmingly negative and the step strictly irreversible.

Step 5: Rapid protonation of $\text{R}_2\text{CH}^-$ delivers the final alkane product $\text{R}_2\text{CH}_2$.

Therefore, the irreversible release of dinitrogen gas ($\text{N}_2$) with large positive entropy provides the primary driving force. Solvent properties or precipitation effects are purely ancillary.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In a Reformatsky reaction, benzaldehyde ($\text{PhCHO}$) is reacted with ethyl 2-bromopropanoate ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH(Br)COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$) in the presence of activated zinc dust in refluxing anhydrous benzene. Subsequent hydrolysis with dilute sulfuric acid yields a $\beta$-hydroxy ester $P$. When ester $P$ is heated in the presence of a catalytic amount of concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, it undergoes dehydration to produce an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ester $Q$. What is the IUPAC name of the major (E)-stereoisomer of compound $Q$?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In the Reformatsky reaction, activated zinc metal inserts oxidative-addition fashion into the carbon-bromine bond of ethyl 2-bromopropanoate to generate the zinc enolate intermediate (Reformatsky reagent):
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(Br)COOEt} + \text{Zn} \longrightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(ZnBr)COOEt} \longleftrightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{C}(\text{OZnBr})\text{OEt}$$

Step 2: The nucleophilic $\alpha$-carbon of this organozinc enolate adds across the carbonyl group of benzaldehyde ($\text{PhCHO}$) via a chair-like six-membered cyclic transition state involving zinc coordination to the carbonyl oxygen. Protonation during mild acidic hydrolysis yields the $\beta$-hydroxy ester ethyl 3-hydroxy-2-methyl-3-phenylpropanoate ($P$):
$$\text{PhCH(OH)}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$$

Step 3: When $\beta$-hydroxy ester $P$ is heated with catalytic concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, protonation of the hydroxyl group followed by loss of water generates a resonance-stabilized carbocation at the benzylic position ($\text{Ph}-\text{CH}^+-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{COOEt}$).

Step 4: Deprotonation at $\text{C}-2$ eliminates a proton to form the conjugated $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ester. Thermodynamic control dictates that the major product adopts the (E)-configuration, in which the bulky phenyl group at $\text{C}-3$ and the bulky ethoxycarbonyl group ($-\text{COOEt}$) at $\text{C}-2$ are oriented trans (anti-periplanar) to each other to minimize steric repulsion.

Step 5: Numbering from the ester carbonyl as $\text{C}-1$, the double bond is between $\text{C}-2$ and $\text{C}-3$, with a methyl substituent at $\text{C}-2$ and a phenyl substituent at $\text{C}-3$. This delivers ethyl (2E)-2-methyl-3-phenylprop-2-enoate ($A$).

Therefore, ethyl (2E)-2-methyl-3-phenylprop-2-enoate is the major stereoisomer. The (Z)-isomer suffers from severe steric clash between the coplanar phenyl and carbethoxy groups, and the other options have invalid IUPAC locants.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The Perkin reaction is a classical synthetic method for the preparation of $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated aromatic carboxylic acids, exemplified by heating benzaldehyde with acetic anhydride in the presence of anhydrous sodium acetate at 180°C. Which of the following statements regarding the mechanism and characteristics of the Perkin reaction is/are TRUE?
options: A) Sodium acetate acts as a base to abstract an $\alpha$-proton from acetic anhydride, generating an anhydride-derived enolate carbanion.
B) Nucleophilic addition of the anhydride enolate to benzaldehyde forms a mixed anhydride $\beta$-alkoxide, which undergoes intramolecular acyl transfer to form an acetoxy intermediate.
C) Dehydration of the intermediate occurs via an E1cB pathway, and subsequent aqueous hydrolysis selectively yields (E)-cinnamic acid as the major thermodynamic product.
D) Replacing benzaldehyde with trimethylacetaldehyde (pivalaldehyde) gives the corresponding $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated carboxylic acid in comparable high yield under identical conditions.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In the Perkin reaction, sodium acetate ($\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$) serves as a weak Brønsted base. It selectively abstracts an $\alpha$-hydrogen from acetic anhydride ($(\text{CH}_3\text{CO})_2\text{O}$) rather than acting as a nucleophile, generating the resonance-stabilized anhydride enolate carbanion ($^-\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{O}-\text{COCH}_3$). Hence, statement A is correct.

Step 2: This enolate carbanion nucleophilically attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon of benzaldehyde ($\text{PhCHO}$) to construct the new carbon-carbon bond, forming a $\beta$-aryl alkoxide. Intramolecular acyl transfer or acetylation by excess acetic anhydride converts this into a $\beta$-acetoxy mixed anhydride intermediate ($\text{PhCH(OAc)}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{O}-\text{COCH}_3$). Hence, statement B is correct.

Step 3: Elimination of acetic acid from the $\beta$-acetoxy intermediate proceeds readily via base-promoted E1cB elimination. The newly formed carbon-carbon double bond adopts the thermodynamically favored trans ((E)) configuration to minimize steric congestion between the phenyl ring and the carbonyl group. Subsequent aqueous hydrolysis of the mixed anhydride liberates (E)-cinnamic acid ($\text{PhCH}=\text{CH}-\text{COOH}$) and acetic acid. Hence, statement C is correct.

Step 4: The Perkin reaction is specifically successful for aromatic aldehydes. Aliphatic aldehydes, even those lacking $\alpha$-hydrogens like pivalaldehyde ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CHO}$), give extremely poor yields or fail entirely under these vigorous conditions (180°C) due to competing aldol-type degradations, ester cleavages, and polymerization. Hence, statement D is incorrect.

Therefore, statements A, B, and C are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In a Knoevenagel condensation, benzaldehyde ($\text{PhCHO}$) is reacted with diethyl malonate ($\text{CH}_2(\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3)_2$) in dry ethanol in the presence of piperidine and a catalytic amount of benzoic acid at reflux to afford an alkylidene diester $X$. Compound $X$ is subsequently hydrolyzed with aqueous potassium hydroxide ($\text{KOH}$) and then heated strongly in dilute sulfuric acid at 180°C. What is the identity of the final organic product $Y$?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Diethyl malonate contains an active methylene group flanked by two electron-withdrawing ester groups ($\text{p}K_a \approx 13$). In the presence of piperidine (a secondary amine base), deprotonation generates the stabilized resonance-delocalized carbanion, which attacks the carbonyl carbon of benzaldehyde.

Step 2: Spontaneous dehydration of the aldol-like carbinol intermediate yields diethyl 2-benzylidenemalonate ($X$, $\text{PhCH}=\text{C}(\text{COOEt})_2$), an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated diester.

Step 3: Alkaline hydrolysis of $X$ with aqueous $\text{KOH}$ saponifies both ethyl ester groups to potassium carboxylates, which upon acidification give 2-benzylidenemalonic acid ($\text{PhCH}=\text{C}(\text{COOH})_2$).

Step 4: 2-benzylidenemalonic acid is a gem-dicarboxylic acid ($\beta$-dicarbonyl acid). Upon heating at 180°C in acidic medium, it undergoes thermal decarboxylation via a concerted cyclic six-membered transition state involving intramolecular hydrogen bonding:
$$\text{PhCH}=\text{C}(\text{COOH})_2 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{PhCH}=\text{CH}-\text{COOH} + \text{CO}_2\uparrow$$

Step 5: The resulting enol intermediate rapidly tautomerizes to the thermodynamically favored (2E)-3-phenylprop-2-enoic acid ($Y$, (E)-cinnamic acid), with the bulky phenyl group and carboxyl group oriented trans to each other.

Therefore, (2E)-3-phenylprop-2-enoic acid is the final product. 2-phenylethanoic acid misses one carbon, 3-phenylpropanoic acid is the saturated analogue requiring catalytic hydrogenation, and 4-phenylbut-3-en-2-one is a ketone obtained from acetone.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: An enantiomerically pure aldehyde, (2R)-2-phenylpropanal ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{Ph})-\text{CHO}$), is reacted with methylmagnesium bromide ($\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$) in anhydrous diethyl ether at $-78^\circ\text{C}$, followed by quenching with saturated aqueous ammonium chloride ($\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$) to yield diastereomeric secondary alcohols of 3-phenylbutan-2-ol according to the Felkin-Anh model. What is the total number of asymmetric chiral carbon centers present in each resulting stereoisomer of 3-phenylbutan-2-ol?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: The starting material is (2R)-2-phenylpropanal, which has the structure:
$$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{Ph})-\text{CHO}$$
Carbon $\text{C}-2$ is an asymmetric chiral carbon center bonded to four distinct substituents: $-\text{H}$, $-\text{CH}_3$, $-\text{Ph}$, and $-\text{CHO}$, configured in the (R) absolute stereochemistry.

Step 2: Nucleophilic addition of the methyl group from $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ occurs at the prochiral formyl carbonyl carbon ($\text{C}-1$). Diastereoselective addition occurs according to the Felkin-Anh transition-state model, converting the planar $sp^2$ carbonyl carbon into an $sp^3$ tetrahedral secondary alcohol center.

Step 3: The resulting alcohol product is 3-phenylbutan-2-ol, whose skeletal structure is:
$$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{Ph})-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}_3$$

Step 4: Now, analyze the asymmetric chiral carbon centers in 3-phenylbutan-2-ol:
- Carbon $\text{C}-3$: Bonded to four distinct groups: $-\text{H}$, $-\text{CH}_3$, $-\text{Ph}$, and $-\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}_3$. This is an asymmetric chiral carbon center.
- Carbon $\text{C}-2$: Bonded to four distinct groups: $-\text{H}$, $-\text{OH}$, $-\text{CH}_3$, and $-\text{CH}(\text{Ph})\text{CH}_3$. This is also an asymmetric chiral carbon center.
- Neither the terminal methyl carbons ($\text{C}-1$ and $\text{C}-4$) nor any phenyl carbons possess four distinct substituents.

Step 5: Thus, each resulting diastereomer contains exactly two asymmetric chiral centers ($\text{C}-2$ and $\text{C}-3$).

Therefore, the total number of asymmetric chiral carbon centers is exactly 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
4-methylpent-3-en-2-one (mesityl oxide, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{CH}-\text{COCH}_3$) is an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone possessing two distinct electrophilic sites. It is subjected to two separate organometallic reactions:
Reaction 1: Mesityl oxide is treated with lithium dimethylcuprate ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CuLi}$, Gilman reagent) in diethyl ether at $0^\circ\text{C}$, followed by mild aqueous acid workup.
Reaction 2: Mesityl oxide is treated with methyllithium ($\text{CH}_3\text{Li}$) in diethyl ether at $-78^\circ\text{C}$, followed by mild aqueous acid workup.
What are the major organic products formed in Reaction 1 and Reaction 2, respectively?
options: C) Both reactions yield 4,4-dimethylpentan-2-one as the thermodynamic product
D) Both reactions yield 2,4-dimethylpent-3-en-2-ol as the kinetic product
questions.explanation:
Step 1: An $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone has two electrophilic centers: the carbonyl carbon ($\text{C}-2$, hard electrophile with higher partial positive charge) and the $\beta$-carbon ($\text{C}-4$, soft electrophile with a larger LUMO coefficient).

Step 2: In Reaction 1, lithium dimethylcuprate ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CuLi}$) is a soft, low-polarity organocopper nucleophile. According to Klopman-Salem frontier molecular orbital theory and the Hard-Soft Acid-Base (HSAB) principle, soft nucleophiles preferentially attack the softer $\beta$-carbon via 1,4-conjugate addition (Michael-type addition).

Step 3: Transfer of a methyl group to the $\beta$-carbon forms an enolate intermediate, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}=\text{C}(\text{O}^-)\text{CH}_3$. Subsequent aqueous protonation gives the saturated ketone 4,4-dimethylpentan-2-one.

Step 4: In Reaction 2, methyllithium ($\text{CH}_3\text{Li}$) is an extremely reactive, hard nucleophile with concentrated negative charge on carbon and significant ionic character. Hard nucleophiles are electrostatically directed to attack the harder carbonyl carbon directly via 1,2-addition.

Step 5: Nucleophilic attack at the carbonyl carbon forms a lithium alkoxide intermediate, which upon aqueous protonation yields the tertiary allylic alcohol 2,4-dimethylpent-3-en-2-ol.

Therefore, Reaction 1 gives 4,4-dimethylpentan-2-one and Reaction 2 gives 2,4-dimethylpent-3-en-2-ol. Reversing these modes of addition overlooks the fundamental difference between hard organolithium reagents and soft organocuprates.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Carbonyl condensation and rearrangement reactions proceed through precisely orchestrated mechanistic steps. Which of the following statements regarding the reaction kinetics and mechanisms of carbonyl transformations is/are TRUE?
options: A) In the Cannizzaro reaction of benzaldehyde, the rate-determining step is the direct intermolecular transfer of a hydride ion from the tetrahedral intermediate to a second molecule of aldehyde.

B) In the base-promoted haloform reaction of acetone, the overall rate of halogenation is first order in acetone and first order in hydroxide, but zero order with respect to the concentration of halogen.
C) In the benzil-benzilic acid rearrangement, nucleophilic attack of hydroxide on one of the carbonyl carbons is followed by an intramolecular 1,2-phenyl shift as the rate-determining step.
D) In the acid-catalyzed aldol condensation of acetone, the rate-determining step is the final dehydration of 4-hydroxy-4-methylpentan-2-one to form mesityl oxide.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In the Cannizzaro reaction of benzaldehyde, hydroxide rapidly adds to benzaldehyde to establish an equilibrium with the hydrated tetrahedral monoanion or dianion. Detailed kinetic isotope studies ($k_{\text{H}}/k_{\text{D}} \approx 2-3$) confirm that the rate-determining step is the intermolecular hydride ion ($\text{H}^-$) transfer from this tetrahedral intermediate to the second aldehyde molecule. Hence, statement A is correct.

Step 2: In the base-promoted haloform reaction of acetone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$), the rate-limiting step is the base-catalyzed abstraction of an $\alpha$-hydrogen by $\text{OH}^-$ to form the enolate ion ($\text{Rate} = k[\text{ketone}][\text{OH}^-]$). Subsequent halogenation of the enolate is extremely rapid. Consequently, the rates of chlorination, bromination, and iodination are identical and completely independent of the concentration and nature of the halogen ($\text{Cl}_2$, $\text{Br}_2$, or $\text{I}_2$). Hence, statement B is correct.

Step 3: In the benzil-benzilic acid rearrangement ($\text{PhCOCOPh} + \text{OH}^- \to \text{Ph}_2\text{C(OH)COO}^-$), hydroxide rapidly attacks one of the carbonyl carbons. The subsequent rate-determining step is the intramolecular 1,2-migration of a phenyl group with its bonding electron pair to the adjacent carbonyl carbon, yielding the potassium benzilate salt. Hence, statement C is correct.

Step 4: In the acid-catalyzed aldol reaction, the rate-determining step is either the slow acid-catalyzed enolization of the ketone or the carbon-carbon bond-forming attack of the enol on the protonated carbonyl. Under strongly acidic conditions, dehydration of the $\beta$-hydroxy ketone is very fast because the hydroxyl group is easily protonated into an excellent leaving group ($-\text{OH}_2^+$). Hence, statement D is incorrect.

Therefore, statements A, B, and C are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When enantiopure (2S)-2-chloropropanal is treated with ethylmagnesium bromide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{MgBr}$) in dry diethyl ether at $-78^\circ\text{C}$ followed by aqueous ammonium chloride workup, nucleophilic addition proceeds with high diastereoselectivity. According to the Felkin-Anh open-chain transition state model, which of the following conformations and trajectories correctly predicts the major diastereomer?
options: A) The carbonyl oxygen and chlorine atom chelate simultaneously to magnesium to form a rigid cyclic five-membered intermediate prior to attack
B) The nucleophile attacks along the trajectory anti-periplanar to the small hydrogen atom because chlorine attracts the incoming Grignard reagent
C) The carbonyl bond eclipses the largest substituent, and the ethyl group attacks perpendicular to the carbon-chlorine bond
D) The large electronegative chlorine substituent adopts a perpendicular orientation to the carbonyl group, and the ethyl group attacks the carbonyl carbon past the small hydrogen atom
questions.explanation:
Step 1: The Felkin-Anh transition-state model predicts the diastereoselective nucleophilic addition to chiral carbonyl compounds lacking chelation. In (2S)-2-chloropropanal ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(Cl)}-\text{CHO}$), the three substituents on the $\alpha$-chiral center are classified by steric and electronic (polar) size:
- Large ($L$): $-\text{Cl}$ (due to its high electronegativity and low-lying $\sigma^*(\text{C}-\text{Cl})$ LUMO which overlaps favorably with the developing $\pi$-bond)
- Medium ($M$): $-\text{CH}_3$
- Small ($S$): $-\text{H}$

Step 2: In the Felkin-Anh reactive conformation, the large group ($L = -\text{Cl}$) is oriented perpendicular ($90^\circ-100^\circ$) to the carbonyl double bond ($\text{C}=\text{O}$) to minimize unfavorable torsional interactions and maximize stabilization from electron transfer into the $\sigma^*(\text{C}-\text{Cl})$ orbital.

Step 3: The incoming nucleophile (ethyl group from $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{MgBr}$) attacks the carbonyl carbon at the Bürgi-Dunitz trajectory angle ($\approx 107^\circ$) from the face opposite the large chlorine atom.

Step 4: Between the remaining two trajectories, attack past the small hydrogen atom ($S = -\text{H}$) experiences significantly less steric hindrance than attack past the bulkier medium methyl group ($M = -\text{CH}_3$).

Step 5: This favored trajectory leads directly to the predominant diastereomer, (2S,3R)-3-chloropentan-2-ol. Chelation control does not operate here because monodentate ether solvent prevents bidentate coordination, and halogen-chelation to magnesium is extremely weak compared to oxygen or nitrogen chelation.

Therefore, option D correctly describes the Felkin-Anh transition state.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The Beckmann rearrangement is an acid-catalyzed isomerization of ketoximes into substituted amides. Which of the following statements regarding the mechanism, stereospecificity, and applications of the Beckmann rearrangement is/are TRUE?
options: A) The rearrangement is strictly stereospecific, involving the anti-migration of the group oriented trans (anti) to the departing oxime hydroxyl ($-\text{OH}$) group.
B) The migrating group shifts with complete retention of stereochemical configuration at the migrating carbon center.

C) When (E)-acetophenone oxime (in which the phenyl group is anti to the hydroxyl group) is treated with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, N-phenylacetamide (acetanilide) is formed as the sole rearrangement product.
D) Treatment of cyclohexanone oxime with concentrated sulfuric acid induces ring expansion to yield $\varepsilon$-caprolactam, the industrial monomer for Nylon-6.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: The Beckmann rearrangement is catalyzed by strong Brønsted or Lewis acids ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, $\text{PCl}_5$, $\text{SOCl}_2$). Protonation or acylation converts the oxime $-\text{OH}$ into an excellent leaving group ($-\text{OH}_2^+$ or $-\text{OPCl}_4$).

Step 2: Migration of the hydrocarbyl group to nitrogen occurs concertedly with the departure of the leaving group from the back side (anti-periplanar geometry). Only the substituent situated anti (trans) to the leaving group can migrate into the developing $\sigma^*(\text{N}-\text{O})$ orbital. Thus, the rearrangement is strictly stereospecific. Hence, statement A is correct.

Step 3: Because the 1,2-shift is concerted and proceeds via an intramolecular frontside migration onto nitrogen without forming a free planar carbocation, chiral migrating centers migrate with complete $100\%$ retention of configuration. Hence, statement B is correct.

Step 4: In (E)-acetophenone oxime, the phenyl ring is oriented anti to the $-\text{OH}$ group, while the methyl group is syn. Selective anti-migration of the phenyl group onto the nitrogen atom produces the nitrilium intermediate $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{N}^+-\text{Ph}$, which on hydration and tautomerization gives N-phenylacetamide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CONHPh}$, acetanilide). Hence, statement C is correct.

Step 5: For cyclic ketoximes like cyclohexanone oxime, anti-migration of the ring carbon concertedly breaks a carbon-carbon bond of the six-membered ring and forms a seven-membered cyclic amide (lactam). This reaction industrially produces $\varepsilon$-caprolactam, which is polymerized to make Nylon-6. Hence, statement D is correct.

Therefore, all statements A, B, C, and D are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In a Reformatsky condensation, 2-methylpropanal ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCHO}$) is reacted with ethyl 2-bromobutanoate ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(Br)COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$) in the presence of activated zinc in anhydrous tetrahydrofuran (THF), followed by mild hydrolysis with dilute aqueous ammonium chloride ($\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$) to yield the $\beta$-hydroxy ester $P$. How many asymmetric chiral carbon centers are present in one molecule of compound $P$?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Ethyl 2-bromobutanoate has the structure $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{COOEt}$. Zinc metal inserts into the carbon-bromine bond to form the Reformatsky zinc enolate:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{ZnBr})\text{COOEt} \longleftrightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}=\text{C}(\text{OZnBr})\text{OEt}$$

Step 2: Nucleophilic addition of this enolate to the carbonyl carbon of 2-methylpropanal ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-\text{CHO}$) followed by protonation delivers the $\beta$-hydroxy ester $P$:
$$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3)-\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$$

Step 3: Analyze each carbon atom in the molecule for stereogenic asymmetry:
- Carbon $\text{C}-3$ of the ester chain (bearing the $-\text{OH}$ group): Attached to $-\text{H}$, $-\text{OH}$, $-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ (isopropyl), and $-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3)\text{COOEt}$. All four attached groups are constitutionally distinct $\implies$ Asymmetric chiral carbon center 1.
- Carbon $\text{C}-2$ of the ester chain (the $\alpha$-carbon): Attached to $-\text{H}$, $-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (ethyl), $-\text{COOEt}$, and $-\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$. All four attached groups are constitutionally distinct $\implies$ Asymmetric chiral carbon center 2.
- The isopropyl methine carbon: Attached to $-\text{H}$, $-\text{CH}(\text{OH})\dots$, and two identical methyl groups ($-\text{CH}_3$). Because two ligands are identical, it is achiral.
- The ethyl methylene carbon and ethoxy methylene carbon are each bonded to two hydrogens and are achiral.

Step 4: Therefore, exactly 2 asymmetric chiral carbon centers exist in compound $P$.

Thus, the integer answer is exactly 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When acetophenone ($\text{PhCOCH}_3$) is treated with ethyl chloroacetate ($\text{ClCH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$) in the presence of sodium ethoxide ($\text{NaOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$) in ethanol at 0°C, a condensation reaction known as the Darzens reaction takes place. What is the structural classification of the primary organic product obtained from this reaction?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: The Darzens reaction involves the base-promoted condensation of an $\alpha$-halo ester with an aldehyde or ketone to synthesize an $\alpha,\beta$-epoxy ester (commonly called a glycidic ester).

Step 2: Sodium ethoxide abstracts an $\alpha$-hydrogen from ethyl chloroacetate ($\text{ClCH}_2\text{COOEt}$) to form the resonance-stabilized carbanion $\text{Cl}-\bar{\text{C}}\text{H}-\text{COOEt}$.

Step 3: This chloromethyl carbanion nucleophilically attacks the carbonyl carbon of acetophenone ($\text{PhCOCH}_3$) to produce a tetrahedral chlorohydrin alkoxide intermediate:
$$\text{Ph}-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)(\text{O}^-)-\text{CH}(\text{Cl})-\text{COOEt}$$

Step 4: The alkoxide oxygen atom then undergoes an intramolecular nucleophilic substitution ($S_N2$-like displacement) attacking the adjacent carbon bearing the chloride leaving group from the backside, displacing the chloride ion ($\text{Cl}^-$) and closing a three-membered oxirane ring.

Step 5: The resulting product is ethyl 3-methyl-3-phenyloxirane-2-carboxylate, which belongs to the class of $\alpha,\beta$-epoxy esters (glycidic esters, $D$). Upon alkaline hydrolysis and acid-catalyzed decarboxylation, glycidic esters rearrange into higher aldehydes or ketones.

Therefore, the primary organic product is an $\alpha,\beta$-epoxy ester. A $\beta$-chloro-$\alpha$-hydroxy ester is the open tetrahedral intermediate prior to ring closure, an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ester is the product of Reformatsky dehydration, and a $\beta$-keto ester arises from Claisen ester condensation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The nucleophilic addition of nitrogen derivatives ($\text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{G}$) to aldehydes and ketones represents a fundamental class of reversible transformations. Which of the following statements regarding the mechanisms and pH dependence of these reactions is/are TRUE?
options: A) The reaction of an aldehyde or ketone with a primary aliphatic amine at $\text{pH} \approx 4.5$ proceeds via an initial neutral carbinolamine intermediate to yield an imine (Schiff base).
B) The reaction of cyclohexanone with a secondary amine such as pyrrolidine in the presence of catalytic acid yields an enamine containing a $\text{C}=\text{C}-\text{N}$ conjugated system.
C) At highly acidic conditions ($\text{pH} < 2$), the rate of imine formation decreases sharply because the amine nucleophile is almost completely protonated into an unreactive ammonium salt.

D) At basic conditions ($\text{pH} > 8$), the rate of imine formation drops significantly because the proton concentration is insufficient to catalyze the dehydration of the carbinolamine intermediate.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Nucleophilic addition of primary amines ($\text{R}-\text{NH}_2$) to aldehydes and ketones begins with unshared electron pair attack on the carbonyl carbon to form a dipolar zwitterionic intermediate, which undergoes proton transfer to give a neutral carbinolamine ($\text{R}_2\text{C(OH)}-\text{NHR}'$). Acid-catalyzed loss of water yields the imine ($\text{R}_2\text{C}=\text{NR}'$, Schiff base). Hence, statement A is correct.

Step 2: With secondary amines ($\text{R}_2'\text{NH}$), the carbinolamine intermediate ($\text{R}_2\text{C(OH)}-\text{NR}_2'$) lacks a proton on the nitrogen atom. Consequently, elimination of water cannot form a neutral $\text{C}=\text{N}$ bond and instead proceeds via loss of a proton from the adjacent $\alpha$-carbon, forming an enamine ($\text{C}=\text{C}-\text{NR}_2'$). Hence, statement B is correct.

Step 3: The rate of imine formation shows a classic bell-shaped pH profile with a rate maximum around $\text{pH} \approx 4.5$. In strongly acidic media ($\text{pH} < 2$), the free amine ($\text{R}-\text{NH}_2$) is converted almost entirely into its conjugate acid, the ammonium cation ($\text{R}-\text{NH}_3^+$). Because the ammonium cation lacks a lone pair, it is completely non-nucleophilic, and the rate-determining initial addition step becomes prohibitively slow. Hence, statement C is correct.

Step 4: In basic or neutral media ($\text{pH} > 8$), although free unprotonated amine is abundant, the elimination step requires acid catalysis to convert the poor leaving group $-\text{OH}$ into the good leaving group $-\text{OH}_2^+$. In the absence of sufficient hydronium ions, the dehydration of the carbinolamine becomes rate-limiting and extremely slow. Hence, statement D is correct.

Therefore, all statements A, B, C, and D are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When (2R)-2-methoxy-1-phenylpropan-1-one is reacted with methylmagnesium iodide ($\text{CH}_3\text{MgI}$) in anhydrous diethyl ether at $-20^\circ\text{C}$, the reaction proceeds with high diastereoselectivity governed by Cram's chelation-control model. Which of the following statements correctly describes the conformational organization and stereochemical pathway of this reaction?
options: A) Nucleophilic addition occurs via a planar carbocation intermediate without any participation of the magnesium counterion
B) The magnesium ion coordinates solely to the phenyl ring $\pi$-cloud forming an inverted sandwich complex
C) Magnesium coordinates simultaneously to the carbonyl oxygen and the $\alpha$-methoxy oxygen to form a rigid five-membered cyclic chelate, directing attack to the less hindered face
D) The $\alpha$-methoxy group undergoes rapid $\beta$-elimination before organometallic addition can take place
questions.explanation:
Step 1: The substrate (2R)-2-methoxy-1-phenylpropan-1-one ($\text{Ph}-\text{CO}-\text{CH}(\text{OCH}_3)\text{CH}_3$) possesses two Lewis basic oxygen donor atoms separated by two carbon atoms: the carbonyl oxygen and the $\alpha$-methoxy oxygen atom.

Step 2: In the presence of a Lewis acidic, divalent metal halide such as $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ from $\text{CH}_3\text{MgI}$, both oxygen atoms coordinate simultaneously to the metal center.

Step 3: This bidentate coordination locks the substrate into a rigid, planar five-membered cyclic chelate ring. In this locked chelate conformation, rotation around the $\text{C}_\alpha-\text{C}_{\text{carbonyl}}$ bond is completely frozen.

Step 4: Looking at the two diastereotopic faces of the chelated carbonyl group, one face is sterically shielded by the methyl group attached to the chiral center, while the opposite face exposes only the small hydrogen atom.

Step 5: The nucleophilic methyl group from a second equivalent of Grignard reagent attacks the carbonyl carbon selectively from the less hindered face (past the hydrogen atom), providing high diastereomeric excess according to Cram's chelate rule.

Therefore, option C provides the exact mechanistic description. Carbocation intermediates do not form with Grignard reagents, $\pi$-sandwich complexes are irrelevant to organomagnesium additions, and methoxy elimination does not occur.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The Robinson annulation and conjugate Michael additions are premier synthetic methods for constructing polycyclic ring systems. Which of the following statements regarding these reaction cascades is/are TRUE?
options: A) The Robinson annulation cascade begins with a base-promoted conjugate Michael addition of a ketone enolate to an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone, followed by an intramolecular aldol condensation.

B) In the conjugate addition of diethyl malonate to cyclohex-2-en-1-one in the presence of sodium ethoxide, the resonance-stabilized malonate carbanion attacks selectively at $\text{C}-3$ (the $\beta$-carbon) rather than $\text{C}-1$.
C) The final dehydration step in the Robinson annulation forms a six-membered cyclohex-2-en-1-one ring due to the thermodynamic stability of the conjugated enone system.
D) Conjugate addition of potassium cyanide ($\text{KCN}/\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$) to conjugated enones is completely irreversible and occurs without forming any tetrahedral 1,2-addition side products.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: The Robinson annulation is an established two-stage cascade: (i) Michael addition: A ketone containing active $\alpha$-hydrogens (such as cyclohexanone) is deprotonated by base and attacks an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone (such as methyl vinyl ketone, but-3-en-2-one) via 1,4-conjugate addition to form a 1,5-diketone intermediate; (ii) Intramolecular aldol condensation: The resulting 1,5-diketone undergoes base-promoted intramolecular aldol addition and dehydration. Hence, statement A is correct.

Step 2: In the addition of diethyl malonate to cyclohex-2-en-1-one, the resonance-stabilized malonate carbanion is a soft nucleophile. Under thermodynamic control, soft nucleophiles attack the soft $\beta$-carbon ($\text{C}-3$) of the $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated enone, generating an enolate that on protonation yields 3-(diethoxycarbonylmethyl)cyclohexan-1-one. Hence, statement B is correct.

Step 3: In the Robinson annulation, the intermediate 1,5-diketone can theoretically form several ring sizes, but base-catalyzed intramolecular aldol cyclization selectively constructs a six-membered ring. Subsequent dehydration generates a conjugated cyclohex-2-en-1-one ring system, whose thermodynamic stability and extended conjugation drive the cascade to completion. Hence, statement C is correct.

Step 4: In the hydrocyanation of $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated carbonyl compounds (Nagata reaction / $\text{HCN}$ addition), cyanohydrin formation via 1,2-addition at the carbonyl carbon is often a rapid, reversible kinetic side reaction. Under thermodynamic equilibration, reversible 1,2-adducts decompose and funnel into the more stable 1,4-conjugate addition product. Thus, calling 1,2-addition absent or the process completely irreversible under all conditions is chemically false. Hence, statement D is incorrect.

Therefore, statements A, B, and C are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In a Perkin condensation, benzaldehyde ($\text{PhCHO}$) is heated with propanoic anhydride ($(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO})_2\text{O}$) in the presence of anhydrous sodium propanoate ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COONa}$) at 180°C, followed by acidic aqueous hydrolysis to produce an $\alpha$-methyl-substituted cinnamic acid derivative $M$. What is the total number of $\pi$-bonds present in one molecule of compound $M$?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In the Perkin reaction between benzaldehyde ($\text{PhCHO}$) and propanoic anhydride ($(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO})_2\text{O}$) catalyzed by sodium propanoate, the base selectively abstracts an $\alpha$-proton from the methylene carbon ($-\text{CH}_2-$) of propanoic anhydride.

Step 2: The generated anhydride enolate carbanion ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}^--\text{CO}-\text{O}-\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$) nucleophilically attacks the carbonyl carbon of benzaldehyde.

Step 3: Subsequent intramolecular acyl transfer, dehydration (elimination of propanoic acid), and aqueous hydrolysis of the mixed anhydride yield (2E)-2-methyl-3-phenylprop-2-enoic acid ($M$, also known as $\alpha$-methylcinnamic acid):
$$\text{Ph}-\text{CH}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{COOH}$$

Step 4: Now, systematically count the total number of $\pi$-bonds in one molecule of (2E)-2-methyl-3-phenylprop-2-enoic acid ($M$):
- The phenyl ring ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-$) contains an aromatic sextet with exactly 3 $\pi$-bonds.
- The acyclic carbon-carbon alkene double bond ($-\text{CH}=\text{C}-$) contains exactly 1 $\pi$-bond.
- The carboxylic acid carbonyl group ($-\text{C}(=\text{O})\text{OH}$) contains exactly 1 $\pi$-bond.
- The methyl group, single $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bonds, and $\text{C}-\text{O}$ single bonds contain only $\sigma$-bonds.

Step 5: Total number of $\pi$-bonds:
$$\text{Total } \pi\text{-bonds} = 3 + 1 + 1 = 5$$

Therefore, the total number of $\pi$-bonds is exactly 5.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Aldehydes and ketones exhibit rich and multifaceted oxidation and oxidative-cleavage behaviors. Which of the following statements regarding oxidation and cleavage reactions of carbonyl compounds is/are TRUE?
options: A) Benzaldehyde reduces ammoniacal silver nitrate (Tollens' reagent) to form a metallic silver mirror, but fails to reduce alkaline cupric tartrate (Fehling's solution) under standard conditions.
B) Selenium dioxide ($\text{SeO}_2$) oxidizes acetophenone selectively at the methyl group to form phenylglyoxal ($\text{PhCOCHO}$), preserving the aromatic ring.
C) Severe oxidative cleavage of unsymmetrical ketones with hot alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ occurs via enolization followed by cleavage of the enolic double bond according to Popoff's rule.
D) Baeyer-Villiger oxidation of cyclobutanone with peroxy acids proceeds smoothly with ring expansion to produce $\gamma$-butyrolactone, driven by relief of four-membered ring strain.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Benzaldehyde is an aromatic aldehyde. While it is easily oxidized by Tollens' reagent ($\text{[Ag(NH}_3)_2]^+$) because silver ion is a sufficiently strong oxidizing agent ($E^\circ \approx +0.80\text{ V}$), it does not reduce Fehling's or Benedict's solutions because cupric ion complexed with tartrate is a weaker oxidizing agent that cannot oxidize aromatic aldehydes under standard conditions. Hence, statement A is correct.

Step 2: Selenium dioxide ($\text{SeO}_2$) is a specialized reagent that specifically oxidizes active $\alpha$-methyl or $\alpha$-methylene groups adjacent to carbonyl or alkene functions. Treatment of acetophenone ($\text{PhCOCH}_3$) with $\text{SeO}_2$ converts the methyl group into an aldehyde group, quantitatively yielding phenylglyoxal ($\text{PhCOCHO}$) without affecting the aromatic ring. Hence, statement B is correct.

Step 3: Vigorous oxidation of ketones using hot alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ or concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ requires tautomerization to the enol form. The resulting enolic $\text{C}=\text{C}$ double bond is then oxidatively cleaved. According to Popoff's empirical rule, in the cleavage of unsymmetrical aliphatic ketones, the carbonyl group remains preferentially attached to the smaller alkyl group. Hence, statement C is correct.

Step 4: Cyclobutanone undergoes Baeyer-Villiger oxidation exceptionally rapidly with peroxy acids (such as mCPBA or trifluoroperacetic acid). Insertion of oxygen into the four-membered cyclic ketone expands the ring to form the five-membered cyclic ester $\gamma$-butyrolactone. This transformation is heavily driven by the relief of high ring strain ($\approx 110\text{ kJ/mol}$) present in the four-membered cyclobutanone ring. Hence, statement D is correct.

Therefore, all statements A, B, C, and D are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The base dissociation constant ($K_b$) of aliphatic amines in aqueous solution depends on the interplay of inductive effect ($+I$), steric hindrance, and hydration stabilization of conjugate ammonium ions. For methyl-substituted amines, compare the basicity of (I) $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{NH}$, (II) $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$, (III) $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N}$, and (IV) $\text{NH}_3$ in aqueous medium.
questions.explanation: Step 1: In aqueous medium, basicity is governed by three opposing factors: the $+I$ inductive effect of methyl groups, hydration enthalpy of the conjugate cation, and steric hindrance around nitrogen. Step 2: Hydration stabilizes ammonium cations with more $\text{N}-\text{H}$ bonds: $\text{RNH}_3^+ > \text{R}_2\text{NH}_2^+ > \text{R}_3\text{NH}^+$. In contrast, the inductive effect increases electron density on nitrogen with more alkyl groups: $\text{R}_3\text{N} > \text{R}_2\text{NH} > \text{RNH}_2$. Step 3: For the small methyl group, steric hindrance is relatively minor, so hydration and inductive effects strike an optimal balance in dimethylamine ($2^\circ$). The resulting aqueous basicity order is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{NH} > \text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2 > (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N} > \text{NH}_3$ ($2^\circ > 1^\circ > 3^\circ > \text{NH}_3$), corresponding to $\text{I} > \text{II} > \text{III} > \text{IV}$. Pure inductive ordering predicts $3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ$, which only holds in the gas phase.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When ethyl groups replace methyl groups on nitrogen, increased steric hindrance shifts the balance between steric crowding, inductive effect, and hydration of the conjugate cation. Which of the following gives the correct sequence of decreasing basic strength in aqueous solution for ethyl-substituted amines?
questions.explanation: Step 1: For ethyl-substituted amines in aqueous medium, ethyl groups are larger and exert stronger $+I$ inductive donation than methyl groups, while also increasing steric hindrance. Step 2: The secondary amine $(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_2\text{NH}$ provides an ideal compromise with two ethyl groups offering strong inductive donation and two hydrogen atoms available for stabilizing hydration in the conjugate ammonium ion. Step 3: In the tertiary amine $(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_3\text{N}$, the cumulative inductive push of three ethyl groups outweighs the loss of hydration relative to the primary amine $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$. Therefore, the aqueous basicity sequence is $2^\circ > 3^\circ > 1^\circ > \text{NH}_3$, yielding $(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_2\text{NH} > (\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_3\text{N} > \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 > \text{NH}_3$. Confusing ethyl with the methyl series yields the incorrect $2^\circ > 1^\circ > 3^\circ$ pattern.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: An equimolar mixture of ethanamine ($1^\circ$), $N$-ethylethanamine ($2^\circ$), and $N,N$-diethylethanamine ($3^\circ$) is treated with benzenesulfonyl chloride (Hinsberg's reagent) in excess aqueous potassium hydroxide. The resulting mixture is extracted with diethyl ether. Which of the following correctly describes the chemical species residing in the aqueous layer and the organic layer, respectively?
options: A) Aqueous layer contains unreacted $3^\circ$ amine; organic layer contains both sulfonamide derivatives
B) Aqueous layer contains the sulfonamide of $2^\circ$ amine; organic layer contains $1^\circ$ and $3^\circ$ amines
C) Aqueous layer contains the potassium salt of $N$-ethylbenzenesulfonamide; organic layer contains $N,N$-diethylbenzenesulfonamide and unreacted $3^\circ$ amine
D) Aqueous layer contains both $1^\circ$ and $2^\circ$ sulfonamides; organic layer contains only the $3^\circ$ amine
questions.explanation: Step 1: Primary amine ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$) reacts with benzenesulfonyl chloride ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{SO}_2\text{Cl}$) to yield $N$-ethylbenzenesulfonamide ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{SO}_2\text{NHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$). Due to the strongly electron-withdrawing benzenesulfonyl group, the hydrogen atom on nitrogen is acidic and reacts with aqueous $\text{KOH}$ to produce a water-soluble potassium salt, remaining in the aqueous layer. Step 2: Secondary amine ($(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_2\text{NH}$) reacts to form $N,N$-diethylbenzenesulfonamide ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{SO}_2\text{N}(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_2$), which lacks an acidic $\text{N}-\text{H}$ proton; it is insoluble in alkali and dissolves into the ether organic layer. Step 3: Tertiary amine ($(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_3\text{N}$) has no hydrogen on nitrogen and does not react under basic conditions, dissolving unreacted in the organic layer. Therefore, the aqueous layer contains the potassium salt of $N$-ethylbenzenesulfonamide, while the organic layer contains the $2^\circ$ sulfonamide and $3^\circ$ amine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the constitutional isomers and functional analogue with molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{11}\text{N}$ and $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$: (I) butan-1-amine, (II) $N$-ethylethanamine, (III) $N,N$-dimethylethanamine, and (IV) butan-1-ol. Which of the following gives the correct descending order of their normal boiling points?
questions.explanation: Step 1: Oxygen is more electronegative than nitrogen, making the $\text{O}-\text{H}$ dipole substantially stronger than the $\text{N}-\text{H}$ dipole. Thus, intermolecular hydrogen bonding is strongest in butan-1-ol (b.p. $\approx 117.7^\circ\text{C}$), placing IV highest. Step 2: Comparing isomeric amines of formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{11}\text{N}$, primary amine butan-1-amine possesses two $\text{N}-\text{H}$ bonds per molecule, providing multiple hydrogen bonding sites (b.p. $\approx 77.8^\circ\text{C}$). Step 3: Secondary amine $N$-ethylethanamine has only one $\text{N}-\text{H}$ bond, forming weaker hydrogen bonds (b.p. $\approx 56^\circ\text{C}$). Tertiary amine $N,N$-dimethylethanamine has no $\text{N}-\text{H}$ bond and cannot form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with itself, boiling at only $36^\circ\text{C}$. Therefore, the sequence is $\text{IV} > \text{I} > \text{II} > \text{III}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: An organic compound of molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{11}\text{N}$ is subjected to the Hinsberg test. Determine the total number of constitutional isomers of $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{11}\text{N}$ that react with benzenesulfonyl chloride to form a neutral sulfonamide precipitate that is strictly insoluble in aqueous potassium hydroxide.
questions.explanation: Step 1: Understand the Hinsberg protocol: primary amines form $N$-alkylbenzenesulfonamides that retain an acidic $\text{N}-\text{H}$ proton and dissolve in aqueous $\text{KOH}$; tertiary amines do not react. Secondary amines react with benzenesulfonyl chloride to form $N,N$-dialkylbenzenesulfonamides, which have no acidic hydrogen on nitrogen and are insoluble in aqueous $\text{KOH}$. Step 2: Enumerate all constitutionally isomeric secondary amines having the molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{11}\text{N}$. Step 3: The possible secondary amine isomers are: (1) diethylamine, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-\text{NH}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$; (2) $N$-methylpropan-1-amine, $\text{CH}_3-\text{NH}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$; and (3) $N$-methylpropan-2-amine, $\text{CH}_3-\text{NH}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$. There are exactly 3 such isomers. Therefore, the integer answer is 3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compound $\text{X}$ ($\text{C}_7\text{H}_9\text{N}$) and Compound $\text{Y}$ ($\text{C}_7\text{H}_9\text{N}$) are constitutional isomers. Both react with acetyl chloride to give neutral monoacetyl derivatives. When treated with $\text{NaNO}_2 + \text{HCl}$ at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$, $\text{X}$ dissolves without gas evolution and the resulting solution yields a brilliant scarlet-red dye upon addition of an alkaline solution of $\beta$-naphthol. Under identical conditions, $\text{Y}$ immediately releases a colorless gas with brisk effervescence and gives a neutral oxygenated liquid. Identify compounds $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$.
questions.explanation: Step 1: Monoacetylation indicates that both $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$ possess a primary (or secondary) amino group. Step 2: Reaction of $\text{X}$ with nitrous acid at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$ without gas evolution to form a diazonium salt that couples with alkaline $\beta$-naphthol to form an azo dye proves that $\text{X}$ is a primary aromatic amine where $-\text{NH}_2$ is bonded directly to the ring (e.g., $p$-toluidine). Step 3: Compound $\text{Y}$ reacts with cold nitrous acid with rapid effervescence of nitrogen gas ($\text{N}_2$) to produce benzyl alcohol. This behavior is characteristic of primary aliphatic or benzylic amines (benzylamine, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$). Therefore, $\text{X}$ is $p$-toluidine and $\text{Y}$ is benzylamine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the Hofmann bromamide degradation reaction, a primary carboxamide is converted into a primary amine with one fewer carbon atom: $\text{R}-\text{CONH}_2 + \text{Br}_2 + 4\text{NaOH} \to \text{R}-\text{NH}_2 + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + 2\text{NaBr} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. When optically active $(R)$-2-phenylpropanamide is subjected to this reaction, which product is formed and what is its stereochemical configuration?
options: A) $(S)$-1-phenylethanamine, with inversion of configuration at the migrating carbon
B) $(R)$-1-phenylethanamine, with complete retention of configuration at the migrating carbon
C) Racemic 1-phenylethanamine, via a planar free radical intermediate
D) 2-phenylethanamine, via an un-rearranged deoxygenation pathway
questions.explanation: Step 1: In the Hofmann bromamide degradation, base deprotonates the amide, followed by bromination to yield an $N$-bromoamide intermediate ($\text{R}-\text{CONHBr}$). Step 2: Further base treatment deprotonates the conjugate nitrogen to trigger 1,2-migration of the chiral group $\text{R}$ from the carbonyl carbon to the adjacent electron-deficient nitrogen atom, with simultaneous expulsion of bromide ion, forming an alkyl isocyanate ($\text{R}-\text{N}=\text{C}=\text{O}$). Step 3: This 1,2-rearrangement is intramolecular and concerted; the migrating group does not detach from the molecular framework. Therefore, the migration proceeds with complete retention of stereochemical configuration at the chiral carbon, yielding $(R)$-1-phenylethanamine after hydrolysis. Assuming inversion or racemization mistakenly presumes an intermolecular displacement or planar intermediate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is a premier method for synthesizing pure primary amines without contamination from secondary or tertiary amines. Which of the following amines CANNOT be prepared by this method, and why?
options: A) 2-phenylethanamine, because the benzylic halide is too unreactive toward nucleophilic substitution
B) Propan-1-amine, because the phthalimide anion cannot displace a primary aliphatic bromide
C) Aniline, because bromobenzene cannot undergo bimolecular nucleophilic substitution ($S_N2$) with potassium phthalimide
D) 2-methylpropan-1-amine, because steric hindrance of the isobutyl group prevents imide ring cleavage
questions.explanation: Step 1: In the Gabriel synthesis, potassium phthalimide reacts with an organic halide via a bimolecular nucleophilic substitution ($S_N2$) pathway to produce an $N$-alkylphthalimide. Step 2: Aryl halides such as bromobenzene do not undergo nucleophilic substitution ($S_N2$) under standard conditions because the carbon-halogen bond possesses partial double bond character due to resonance with the benzene ring, the aromatic carbon is $sp^2$ hybridized, and the approaching nucleophile experiences electrostatic repulsion from the benzene $\pi$-electron cloud. Step 3: Because the $S_N2$ step fails for aryl and vinyl halides, aromatic primary amines such as aniline cannot be prepared by the Gabriel synthesis. Primary aliphatic halides (including benzyl and phenylethyl halides) react smoothly.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Aniline reacts with aqueous bromine water at room temperature to yield a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromoaniline quantitatively. To prepare monobromoaniline (predominantly $p$-bromoaniline) in high yield, the activating effect of the $-\text{NH}_2$ group must be modulated. What is the correct sequence of reagents to accomplish this transformation?
questions.explanation: Step 1: The amino group in aniline is strongly activating toward electrophilic aromatic substitution due to resonance donation ($+M$) of the nitrogen lone pair, which causes tri-bromination even with dilute bromine water. Step 2: Acetylation with acetic anhydride in pyridine protects the amino group to form acetanilide ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NHCOCH}_3$). In acetanilide, the nitrogen lone pair is delocalized into the carbonyl oxygen, substantially moderating ring activation. Step 3: Electrophilic bromination of acetanilide with $\text{Br}_2$ in glacial acetic acid occurs selectively at the less sterically hindered para-position to give 4-bromoacetanilide. Subsequent acidic hydrolysis ($\text{H}_3\text{O}^+, \Delta$) removes the acetyl protecting group to furnish $p$-bromoaniline cleanly.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A saturated acyclic monoamine has a vapor density of $36.5$. Reaction of $0.050\text{ mol}$ of this amine with excess acetyl chloride consumes $0.050\text{ mol}$ of acetyl chloride to form a neutral mono-acetylated amide. When $0.100\text{ mol}$ of this amine is treated with cold nitrous acid ($\text{NaNO}_2 / \text{HCl}$), it quantitatively evolves $0.100\text{ mol}$ of nitrogen gas ($\text{N}_2$). Calculate the total number of carbon atoms present in one molecule of this amine.
questions.explanation: Step 1: Saturated acyclic monoamines have the general formula $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+3}\text{N}$. The molecular mass is related to vapor density by: $M = 2 \times \text{Vapor Density} = 2 \times 36.5 = 73.0\text{ g/mol}$. Step 2: Mono-acetylation and quantitative evolution of $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{N}_2$ per mole of amine in cold nitrous acid confirm that the compound is a primary aliphatic monoamine. Step 3: Express the molecular weight in terms of $n$: $12n + (2n + 3) + 14 = 14n + 17$. Setting $14n + 17 = 73$ gives $14n = 56$, which solves to $n = 4$. Therefore, there are exactly 4 carbon atoms in one molecule of this amine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the following reduction reactions designed to prepare primary amines: (I) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NO}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2/\text{Ni}} \text{P}$, (II) $\text{CH}_3\text{CN} \xrightarrow{\text{Na}/\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}} \text{Q}$, and (III) $\text{CH}_3\text{CONH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4/\text{ether},\text{ then }\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{R}$. Which of the following statements correctly identifies products $\text{P}$, $\text{Q}$, and $\text{R}$?
options: A) All three products $\text{P}$, $\text{Q}$, and $\text{R}$ are identical and correspond to ethanamine
B) $\text{P}$ is ethanamine, while $\text{Q}$ and $\text{R}$ are methanamine
C) $\text{P}$ and $\text{Q}$ are ethanamine, but $\text{R}$ is methanamine
D) $\text{P}$ is ethanamine, $\text{Q}$ is methanamine, and $\text{R}$ is ethanol
questions.explanation: Step 1: Catalytic hydrogenation of nitroethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NO}_2$) reduces the nitro group to an amino group with preservation of the two-carbon chain, yielding ethanamine ($\text{P} = \text{ethanamine}$). Step 2: Mendius reduction of acetonitrile ($\text{CH}_3\text{CN}$) using sodium in boiling ethanol adds four hydrogen atoms across the $\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$ triple bond to produce ethanamine ($\text{Q} = \text{ethanamine}$). Step 3: Reduction of acetamide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CONH}_2$) by lithium aluminium hydride ($\text{LiAlH}_4$) reduces the carbonyl group ($-\text{CO}-$) to a methylene group ($-\text{CH}_2-$) without carbon loss, producing ethanamine ($\text{R} = \text{ethanamine}$). Thus, all three products are identical to ethanamine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the carbylamine reaction (isocyanide test), an aliphatic or aromatic primary amine reacts with chloroform in the presence of ethanolic potassium hydroxide to produce a characteristic disagreeable odor. What is the reactive electrophilic intermediate generated in this reaction, and which of the following amines will give a positive test?
options: A) Dichloromethyl cation ($\text{CHCl}_2^+$); gives positive test with $N$-methylaniline
B) Dichlorocarbene ($:\text{CCl}_2$); gives positive test with aniline
C) Trichloromethyl carbanion ($:\text{CCl}_3^-$); gives positive test with triethylamine
D) Dichlorocarbene ($:\text{CCl}_2$); gives positive test with $N,N$-dimethylaniline
questions.explanation: Step 1: Strong base ($\text{OH}^-$) abstracts the proton from chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$) to form the trichloromethyl carbanion ($:\text{CCl}_3^-$), which subsequently loses a chloride ion via $\alpha$-elimination to generate neutral, electron-deficient dichlorocarbene ($:\text{CCl}_2$). Step 2: Dichlorocarbene has a vacant $p$-orbital and acts as an electrophile that is attacked by the nucleophilic nitrogen of primary amines. Step 3: Subsequent base-induced eliminations of two molecules of $\text{HCl}$ afford the alkyl or aryl isocyanide (carbylamine). Secondary and tertiary amines lack two protons on nitrogen and cannot form isocyanides. Therefore, the intermediate is dichlorocarbene, and aniline (a primary aromatic amine) gives a positive test.

questions.subject: Chemistry
